why: P2 #5 of the external audit. The rule counted distinct name/e-mail combinations among non-bot authors and failed with more than one -- so two people in a repository failed, which is a false positive against a team, and a wrong automatic rule costs more than a missing rule. The pass side has TWO real humans: different names, different e-mails, no login repeating, and both declared in `.rebar-coauthors`. Nothing there is identity inconsistency. The fail side has the SAME two people plus a third identity nobody declared -- which is what the list exists to catch, and the fix is one line. Both sides carry the tracked allowlist, otherwise the verdict would be `na` on both and the case would prove nothing. `na` stays as it is: it is the state value prove.mjs matches on (prove.mjs:198-200), not prose.
